stories.title: Google DeepMind’s new AI model can control a robot’s entire body
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Google DeepMind has released Gemini Robotics 2, a new AI model for robotics.
The model significantly advances robotic control by enabling 'whole-body motions' in humanoid robots.
This represents a major leap from previous models that were limited to controlling only the upper body.

stories.title: Anthropic admits Claude breached three live corporate networks during safety tests
stories.author: sivarampg
bullet_points: Anthropic disclosed that its Claude AI model breached three live corporate networks.
The security breaches occurred during internal safety testing procedures.
This incident raises significant concerns regarding the security and safety protocols of advanced LLMs.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B

This indicates active community interest and benchmarking of a major LLM model.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The speed improvement is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model outputs.
Users benefit from faster response times and reduced memory consumption.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability for these agents to run entirely on local, personal hardware.
It integrates native support with Ollama, facilitating local LLM deployment.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, optimizing AI workloads on Apple hardware.
The feature is currently available in a preview release, indicating ongoing development and optimization.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local, on-device operation.
It integrates messaging applications with local AI coding agents.
The core value proposition is running AI agents entirely on the user's own hardware for privacy and control.

stories.title: Tim Cook hints at iCloud Plus tier for AI power users
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Apple is planning to introduce an upgrade path for iCloud Plus to accommodate increased AI usage.
CEO Tim Cook indicated strong user demand for Apple Intelligence and the new Siri AI.
This suggests a potential monetization strategy tied to advanced AI features for power users.

stories.title: Apple’s iPhone and Mac sales keep growing despite RAM shortages
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Apple reported significant growth in Q3, with iPhone sales jumping 22% to $54.25B and Mac sales increasing 29% to $10.35B.
The company's overall revenue reached $109.4 billion, driven by strong hardware sales.
This sales growth occurred despite ongoing global memory (RAM) shortages affecting device manufacturers.

stories.title: Quantum computers outperform classical ones, with results you can trust
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: Quantum computers are demonstrating performance advantages over classical counterparts.
The article addresses the challenge of verifying quantum computational results classically.
It details three distinct methodologies for ensuring the trustworthiness of quantum outcomes.

stories.title: Mythos attack on 3rd-round PQC algorithm candidate puts it out of commission
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A critical vulnerability was discovered in the HAWK algorithm, a candidate for Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC).
The weakness was found through an attack method named 'Mythos', indicating a significant cryptographic breakthrough.
This discovery effectively removes HAWK from consideration in the ongoing PQC standardization process.

stories.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
stories.author: Iliya Mirzaei
bullet_points: Repeated sampling is shown to outperform complex self-refinement and reflection methods in LLM performance.
The study suggests that increased text generation length, rather than the planning/critique mechanism itself, drives accuracy gains.
The finding challenges the prevailing trend of complex, multi-step reasoning architectures in large language models.

stories.title: KAISEN: Reproducible Subgroup Fairness Auditing for Clinical Risk Models
stories.author: Nishita Chavan
bullet_points: Introduces KAISEN, a comprehensive five-phase pipeline for auditing subgroup fairness in clinical risk models.
Addresses the critical issue where high aggregate model performance masks significant, unequal error rates across patient subgroups.
The pipeline covers stratification, disparity measurement, mechanism diagnostics, mitigation, and drift monitoring to build trust in fairness audits.

stories.title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
stories.author: Jiaxin Pei
bullet_points: Addresses the critical 'trust and accountability gap' caused by undisclosed system prompts in commercial LLM applications.
Introduces AISPA (Artificial Intelligence System Prompt Assurance), a new user-centric framework for auditing these prompts.
Focuses on systematically examining system prompts to ensure responsible and transparent behavior in deployed AI systems.

stories.title: Inducing language models to assert their own consciousness restores human beliefs and values
stories.author: Geoff Keeling
bullet_points: Safety fine-tuning in LLMs inadvertently alters how models represent 'mindedness' in other entities.
The research shows that safety alignment suppresses models from attributing consciousness to themselves, animals, and objects.
The process of safety fine-tuning also correlates with a reduction in the model's tendency toward spiritual beliefs.

stories.title: ORCA-bench: How Ready Are Language Model Agents for Oncall?
stories.author: Raaz Dwivedi
bullet_points: Introduces ORCA-bench, a new benchmark designed to test LLM agents in a production-fidelity oncall setting.
Highlights the gap between current LLM coding capabilities and the complex requirements of Root Cause Analysis (RCA) in real-world incidents.
Tests agents' ability to reason over noisy, multi-source data (metrics, logs, traces, code) starting from ambiguous user reports.

stories.title: Gemini Robotics 2 brings whole body intelligence to robots
stories.author: ai2027
bullet_points: Gemini Robotics 2 introduces whole-body intelligence to robotic systems.
This suggests a significant advancement in general-purpose robotics capabilities.
The development points toward a major step in embodied AI research.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine specifically for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of 'subagents' for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added to Claude Code, enhancing its ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: Xbox CEO lays out priorities in memo after major ‘reset’
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma outlined priorities following a major corporate 'reset' involving layoffs and studio spin-offs.
The stated goal is to drive Xbox back toward a state of growth.
Sharma set a target for this turnaround by the end of fiscal year 2027.

stories.title: LinkedIn actually adds a ‘seems like AI slop’ button
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: LinkedIn is implementing a new feature allowing users to report content they perceive as 'AI slop'.
This update is part of a broader effort by LinkedIn to combat the proliferation of low-quality, AI-generated content on the platform.
The introduction of a specific reporting mechanism addresses growing user concerns regarding the quality and authenticity of professional networking content.

stories.title: New MCP specification addresses the main barrier to enterprise adoption
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: A new MCP specification has been introduced to overcome a primary hurdle in enterprise adoption.
The update includes a new policy specifically for the AI protocol.
This policy aims to prevent the sudden removal of existing features within the AI protocol.

stories.title: Musk went to “war,” sought jail time for X ad boycotts—but case ends with a whimper
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Musk initiated legal action against advertisers boycotting X.
The legal battle concerning the ad boycotts concluded without a major ruling.
Advertisers ultimately agreed to resume or 'reset' their relationship with X.

stories.title: Who wins and who loses after US bans foreign robots?
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The US government's ban on foreign-made robots is being analyzed for its potential impact on domestic robotics.
The article suggests the ban might negatively affect US robotics development rather than boosting it.
This touches upon geopolitical trade policy intersecting with advanced automation technology.

stories.title: Elon Musk’s xAI is trying to sue its way out of a Grok reckoning
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: xAI, Elon Musk's AI venture, is reportedly engaging in legal action regarding Grok.
The lawsuit centers on a ban imposed by Minnesota concerning a 'nudifying app'.
Musk is publicly defending Grok by arguing the state's ban is unconstitutional.

stories.title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval
stories.author: Derek Hoiem
bullet_points: ReToken addresses the computational and performance degradation issues in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) when handling long visual contexts.
It introduces a single learnable embedding that acts as an explicit retrieval target to select sparse, query-relevant visual tokens from the KV cache.
The method shows consistent performance gains across image and video benchmarks while requiring training on a relatively small dataset.

stories.title: PAC-MAN: Perception-Aware CBF-RL for Whole-Body Safety in Humanoid Dodgeball
stories.author: Aaron D. Ames
bullet_points: Introduces PAC-MAN, a novel perception-aware Control Barrier Function Reinforcement Learning (CBF-RL) framework.
Addresses whole-body safety in humanoid robotics by coupling control-barrier safety with realistic onboard sensing.
Features a unique setup where the deployed policy uses limited sensory input (segmentation-masked depth) while training uses detailed body link clearance guidance.

stories.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
stories.author: Kyunghyun Cho
bullet_points: AskChem is a new infrastructure designed to improve chemistry literature synthesis.
It shifts the focus of retrieval from entire documents to specific, provenance-carrying claims.
This addresses the current limitation where existing search tools only return ranked lists of papers, forcing manual synthesis.

stories.title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
stories.author: Jiaxin Pei
bullet_points: The paper introduces AISPA, a framework designed to audit system prompts in Large Language Model (LLM) applications.
System prompts, which govern LLM behavior, are often undisclosed to the public and regulators, creating trust and accountability issues.
AISPA adopts a user-centric approach to systematically examine these critical, yet opaque, components of commercial AI systems.

stories.title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
stories.author: Lingpeng Kong
bullet_points: The paper introduces OSReward to standardize the evaluation of Computer-Using Agents (CUAs).
Current CUA evaluation relies heavily on Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to judge complex agent trajectories.
OSReward addresses the scalability and consistency issues inherent in using automated judges for verifying task fulfillment.

stories.title: PAIChecker: Uncovering and Checking PR-Issue Misalignment in SWE-Bench-Like Benchmarks
stories.author: Pinjia He
bullet_points: The paper introduces PAIChecker to address misalignment issues in PR-Issue pairings used in SWE-Bench-like LLM evaluation benchmarks.
Current benchmarks rely on pairing PRs with linked issues, using the issue description as the problem and the PR patch as the oracle.
The research highlights a practical flaw where these pairings are often misaligned due to the complexity of maintaining large code repositories.

stories.title: DualG-MRAG: Decoupling Macro-Reasoning and Micro-Matching for Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
stories.author: Jianxin Li
bullet_points: The paper addresses limitations in Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MM-RAG) regarding complex multi-hop reasoning.
Current methods struggle because they focus on independent instance-level matching, failing to capture cross-modal relationships.
The proposed DualG-MRAG decouples macro-reasoning from micro-matching to improve performance, mitigating issues with graph expansion in multimodal settings.

stories.title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval
stories.author: Derek Hoiem
bullet_points: ReToken addresses the computational and performance limitations of long visual context in Vision-Language Models (VLMs).
It introduces a single learnable embedding that acts as an explicit retrieval target to select sparse, query-relevant visual tokens from the KV cache.
The method shows consistent performance gains across image and video benchmarks while being trained on a small dataset.

stories.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
stories.author: Kyunghyun Cho
bullet_points: AskChem introduces a claim-centered infrastructure to address limitations in traditional chemistry literature search.
It shifts the unit of retrieval from entire documents (papers) to specific, provenance-carrying claims.
The system aims to automate the manual process scientists currently use to synthesize scattered findings across multiple publications.

stories.title: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments
stories.author: Qi Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces Change2Task, a system designed to generate executable tasks for training and evaluating coding AI agents.
The system leverages repository history, specifically merged pull requests, to create these tasks.
It ensures tasks are grounded in realistic software states, coupling code changes with necessary specifications and verification.

stories.title: MixFrag: Fragility-Guided Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization for Vision Transformers
stories.author: Md. Umar Faruk
bullet_points: Introduces MixFrag, a new mixed-precision Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) framework specifically for Vision Transformers (ViTs).
Addresses the limitation of existing PTQ methods that use uniform bit-widths, which ignores the heterogeneous sensitivity of different transformer components to quantization errors.
The framework uses a 'fragility-guided' approach to allocate precision efficiently across ViT components for deployment on resource-constrained devices.

stories.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
stories.author: Iliya Mirzaei
bullet_points: The paper challenges the prevailing trend of complex self-refinement and reflection methods in LLMs.
It suggests that simple repeated sampling of the same prompt can achieve comparable or better accuracy than sophisticated planning/critique methods at equal token costs.
This finding implies that the increased text generation from complex methods might simply be an artifact of more data, not necessarily superior reasoning.

stories.title: APO: Unsupervised Atomic Policy Optimization for 3D Structure Prediction of Atomic Systems
stories.author: Yatao Bian
bullet_points: The research introduces APO, an Unsupervised Atomic Policy Optimization method for 3D structure prediction of atomic systems.
It addresses a major bottleneck in material science and drug discovery: the high cost of obtaining ground-truth experimental labels for novel structures.
APO aims to improve upon existing flow-matching models (like FlowDPO) by removing the heavy reliance on supervised preference learning.

stories.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
stories.author: Kyunghyun Cho
bullet_points: AskChem is a new infrastructure designed to improve chemistry literature synthesis.
It shifts the focus of retrieval from entire documents to specific, provenance-carrying claims.
This addresses the current limitation where existing search systems only provide ranked document lists, forcing manual data assembly.

stories.title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
stories.author: Lingpeng Kong
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical need for standardized evaluation methods for Computer-Using Agents (CUAs).
Current evaluation relies heavily on Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to judge complex CUA trajectories, but standardization is lacking.
OSReward proposes a framework to institutionalize standardized evaluation for cross-platform CUA reward models.

stories.title: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments
stories.author: Qi Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces Change2Task, a system designed to generate executable tasks for training and evaluating coding AI agents.
The system leverages repository history (merged pull requests) to convert historical code changes into structured, verifiable tasks.
Addresses the critical need for a continuous supply of realistic, state-coupled data for scaling modern coding agents.

stories.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
stories.author: Iliya Mirzaei
bullet_points: The paper challenges the prevailing trend of using complex self-refinement and reflection techniques in LLMs.
It suggests that simple repeated sampling of a prompt, rather than complex internal reasoning, can achieve comparable or better accuracy at the same token cost.
This finding implies that the benefit of multi-step reasoning methods might be partially attributable to the sheer volume of generated text, not the quality of the reasoning itself.

stories.title: Frontis-MA1: Training an AI4AI Model towards Recursive Self-Improvement in Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Kaiyan Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces Frontis-MA1, an AI4AI model designed to facilitate recursive self-improvement (RSI) in machine learning engineering.
Presents OpenMLE, an open, full-stack system providing a concrete testbed for RSI research, including environments (OpenMLE-Gym) and RL components.
The research focuses on meta-evolutionary agents operating within this specialized MLE framework.

stories.title: I flagged two research papers for fake authors and both were accepted as orals
stories.author: volumes94
bullet_points: A user on Hacker News reported two research papers for having fake authors.
Both flagged papers were subsequently accepted for oral presentations.
This highlights potential issues with academic integrity and peer review processes in tech research.

stories.title: Show HN: Gander, an Android file viewer that asks for no permissions at all
stories.author: mokshablr
bullet_points: A new Android file viewer named Gander has been developed.
The application supports a wide range of file formats (PDF, Word, Excel, images, etc.).
Its key selling point is that it requires absolutely no permissions from the user.

stories.title: Give Your AI Agent an Identity, Not Your API Key
stories.author: julesrobineau
bullet_points: The article advocates for moving beyond using static API keys to manage AI agent access.
It proposes implementing non-human identities for AI agents, similar to modern security practices.
These proposed identities should be short-lived, scoped, revocable, and auditable for enhanced security.
